name: Resideo Technologies, Inc.

profile.description: Resideo Technologies, Inc. is a global provider of smart home and building technology solutions, spun off from Honeywell in 2018. It operates in two segments: Products & Solutions (P&S), which develops thermostats, security and fire safety products, and connected home devices under the Honeywell Home brand; and ADI Global Distribution, a leading wholesale distributor of low-voltage security, fire, AV, and networking products. Q1 2026 revenue was $1.9B (+8% YoY) with Adj EBITDA of $215M (+20%). Q2 decelerated to $2.0B (+2%) with EPS of $0.51 missing estimates. ADI spin-off into independent public company expected by late 2026.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Resideo executed meaningful strategic transformations — the major acquisition that expanded ADI Global Distribution into a ~$5B distributor, and the planned spin-off into two focused public companies (Form 10 filed) demonstrate active business model evolution [1]. Q1 2026 P&S revenue grew 9% YoY with 12 consecutive quarters of margin expansion to 25.1% adjusted EBITDA margin, though Q2 decelerated to 2% overall growth [1]. AI Deployment (1/2): The ProSeries security platform integrates AI for advanced video analytics and false alarm reduction, shipping to customers as a measurable AI-enhanced product, though AI-specific revenue has not been separately quantified [4]. Market Share (1/2): ADI is a market-leading distributor in low-voltage security and AV products, and P&S commands strong share in residential thermostats and fire safety under the Honeywell Home brand. Product Pipeline (1/2): ADI spin-off completion expected by late 2026, plus plans to embed AI across product lines for predictive home management. CDO hired to lead technology roadmap [3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Active embedded technology development for smart home and energy-efficient products positions Resideo above industrial distribution peers.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Resideo's core values — 'Start with the Customer, Act as One Team, Pioneer the Future, and Make a Difference' — are specific and thoughtful, reflecting genuine intentionality about building smarter, safer home environments that connect the company's work to family protection and sustainability [5]. Community Impact (1/2): The company invested nearly $5M in sustainability CapEx including CO2e reduction projects, achieved EcoVadis Silver Medal (top 8% of peer category), and publishes comprehensive ESG reports with long-term environmental targets [6]. Employee Retention (2/2): Exceptional Glassdoor scores — 4.5/5 stars based on 636+ reviews with 89% recommending the company, culture and values rated 4.4/5, work-life balance 4.4/5 [4]. Employees describe innovative culture with good work-life balance. CEO Jay Geldmacher's 6+ year tenure provides leadership stability. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying by executives identified in the last 12 months despite the stock's 48% decline from $36 to $18.88.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on Growth metrics. GAAP metrics have normalized significantly as the $1.59B Honeywell indemnification payment distortion fades — ROE has recovered to 15.2% (at the 15% target, scoring 1.0 with 2x weight), and profit margin has turned positive at 5.58% (score 0.28), both massive improvements from the prior report's -16.93% ROE and -7.05% margin [2]. D/E of 129.9% (score 0.74) reflects remaining acquisition debt. Revenue growth decelerated from Q1's 8% to Q2's 2% (score 0.73 on trailing 2% YoY), and estimated 5yr CAGR of ~7% scores 0.80 (2x weight). Forward P/E of 9.19 is deeply below the 20 target (score 1.0) — the stock's 48% decline from $36 to $18.88 has created compelling valuation [2]. FY2026 guidance of $7.8-7.9B revenue and $3.00-3.20 adjusted EPS implies the stock trades at 6x adjusted forward earnings. PEG unavailable, excluded. Weighted sum 6.35/8.0. Liquidity: 2,543,106 avg volume x $18.88 = $48.0M, well above floor.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Resideo's core business involves physical-world products — thermostats, security panels, fire safety devices, and wholesale distribution of low-voltage hardware — that AI structurally cannot displace; these products require physical installation, wiring, and maintenance in homes and buildings [1]. AI actually increases demand for Resideo's offerings by enabling smarter home automation, predictive maintenance, and enhanced security analytics. ADI's distribution network of physical warehouses and installer relationships creates moats AI cannot replicate. However, smart home competitive dynamics from Ring/Amazon, Google Nest, and Alarm.com with larger AI platforms create some competitive pressure [3]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Resideo ships AI-powered products through the ProSeries platform with advanced video analytics and false alarm reduction, and plans to embed AI across product lines for predictive home management [4].

infinite_game.summary: Resideo demonstrates strong infinite game characteristics under CEO Jay Geldmacher's 6+ year tenure. The $1.59B Honeywell payment to eliminate perpetual indemnification obligations is a textbook example of courage to lead — sacrificing short-term financials for long-term strategic freedom. The ADI spin-off reflects willingness to reshape the business for focus rather than cling to size. Exceptional Glassdoor scores (4.5/5, 89% recommend) indicate genuine organizational trust. The gap is the absence of a transcendent Just Cause — the company's purpose is specific and thoughtful but not a vision that can never be fully achieved.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Resideo's vision of making homes smarter, safer, and more sustainable is genuine and connects to meaningful purpose — particularly through fire safety, security, and energy efficiency products that protect families [5]. The core values 'Pioneer the Future' and 'Make a Difference' have substance backed by Honeywell heritage and active product innovation. However, it remains a technology-product mission rather than a transcendent cause that can never be fully achieved.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): The $1.59B one-time payment to Honeywell to permanently terminate the Indemnification Agreement is a defining act of courage — management absorbed a massive near-term financial hit (driving FY2025 GAAP net loss of $527M) to eliminate a perpetual liability that would have constrained the company indefinitely [1]. The ADI spin-off demonstrates willingness to make painful structural choices for long-term strategic focus over short-term revenue scale. Q2 2026 operating profit declined 26% YoY as the company prioritizes long-term transformation over near-term optics [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (2/2): Exceptional organizational trust evidenced by Glassdoor 4.5/5 stars with 89% recommending the company, culture and values rated 4.4/5, and work-life balance at 4.4/5 based on 636+ reviews [4]. Employees describe 'Great work culture with technologies to learn and explore' and 'innovative and good work life balance.' CEO Geldmacher's 6+ year tenure provides leadership stability during a period of significant transformation including the Honeywell payment and ADI spin-off preparation.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Resideo has demonstrated incremental flexibility — spun off from Honeywell in 2018, expanded ADI through major acquisition, and now plans to spin off ADI as an independent public company by late 2026 to create two focused entities [3]. These are significant structural changes but follow conventional industrial conglomerate logic rather than cause-driven transformation. The company has reshaped its portfolio twice in under a decade, showing willingness to evolve.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Resideo's public communications focus on its market position and competitive advantages rather than acknowledging what it can learn from rivals like Alarm.com, Ring/Amazon, or Google Nest in the smart home space [3]. The SEC filing notes competitors 'may incorporate AI into their products more quickly,' but this is framed as a threat rather than motivation for self-improvement.

investment_thesis: Resideo at $18.88 and 9.19x forward earnings (or ~6x adjusted EPS guidance of $3.00-3.20) presents a compelling value opportunity as GAAP metrics normalize post-Honeywell payment. ROE has recovered to 15.2% from -16.93% and profit margin has turned positive at 5.58%, reflecting the underlying business health obscured by the one-time $1.59B charge [2]. Q1 2026 was strong: total revenue of $1.912B (+8% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA of $215M (+20%) and P&S achieving 25.1% adjusted EBITDA margin in its 12th consecutive quarter of expansion [1]. The ADI spin-off (Form 10 filed, expected late 2026) should unlock sum-of-the-parts value — ADI alone generates ~$5B in revenue while P&S delivers ~$2.8B at 25%+ EBITDA margins. AI integration into ProSeries positions Resideo for smart home market growth. Glassdoor scores of 4.5/5 with 89% recommendation rate indicate exceptional organizational health [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on the Q2 deceleration and leverage. Q2 2026 revenue grew only 2% (vs Q1's 8%), operating profit fell 26% YoY, and EPS of $0.51 badly missed estimates of $0.69, driving the 48% stock decline from $36 to $18.88 [1][3]. D/E of 129.9% reflects $936M+ in total debt from the Honeywell payment and ADI acquisition, creating deleveraging pressure that limits capital allocation flexibility. The ADI spin-off introduces execution complexity — separating a ~$5B distribution business involves IT, supply chain, and organizational untangling that could distract management. Revenue is ~50% tied to home improvement and construction activity vulnerable to housing market weakness. Smart home competitors (Ring/Amazon, Google Nest, Alarm.com) have larger platforms and deeper AI investment budgets. The negative book value of -$13.76/share (total equity -$445M) means no balance sheet cushion in a downturn, though this is a GAAP artifact of the Honeywell payment.
key_catalysts: ADI spin-off completion expected late 2026, creating two focused public companies and unlocking sum-of-the-parts value — at $18.88, the combined entity trades at ~6x adjusted earnings guidance of $3.00-3.20 [1][3]

GAAP metric normalization as Honeywell payment distortion fully rolls off — trailing ROE of 15.2% and positive profit margin signal the underlying business quality that was masked by the one-time $1.59B charge [2]
P&S margin expansion trajectory (12 consecutive quarters to 25.1% adjusted EBITDA margin) and AI-enhanced ProSeries product launches driving higher-margin product mix [1][4]
key_risks: Q2 revenue deceleration to 2% growth with EPS miss ($0.51 vs $0.69 estimate) suggests demand softening that could continue into H2 2026, potentially forcing guidance reductions from the $3.00-3.20 adjusted EPS range [1][3]

Leverage with D/E of 129.9% and negative book value of -$13.76/share creates financial fragility — $936M+ in debt requires disciplined deleveraging that limits strategic flexibility during the ADI separation [2]

Housing market sensitivity with ~50% of revenue tied to home improvement and construction activity — rising rates or consumer spending weakness could compress both P&S product demand and ADI distributor volumes [1]
